city_metadata.title: EXPLAINITARIUM
city_metadata.subtitle: A map that explains how it was made · metropolis-kit + deckcast
city_metadata.scale_axis_description: South to north: a document nobody reads → agents that understand it → a compiler that builds views → voices that tell it → maps already in use.

districts.name: 1 · THE DOCUMENT
districts.description: Real sources that were explained with this kit: a report chapter, a research paper, a project canvas.

districts.name: 2 · UNDERSTANDING
districts.description: Two agents turn a document into a one-page profile and then a semantic spec; a person approves both and a provenance file keeps every number honest.

districts.name: 3 · BUILDING
districts.description: A deterministic compiler turns the spec into a 3D city, a metro map and a guided tour.

districts.name: 4 · VOICE
districts.description: deckcast voices the tour as a dialogue; then pre-voiced questions; then a live agent that answers and moves the map.

districts.name: 5 · IN USE
districts.description: Maps and narrated decks that exist today.

spires.title: SCIANCE D1.1 — Materials Science chapter
spires.abstract: A landscape report chapter on AI in European materials science, revised three times while the map followed it. The kind of document reviewers skim and nobody reads to page 47.

spires.title: arXiv:2609.11975 — AI-Research Agents in the Wild
spires.abstract: A meta-study of the public ecosystem of AI-research agents, with six candidate regularities, a prospective audit and three supplementary tables. Its argument lives in tables and caveats.

spires.title: Knowledge Discovery — CEO status canvas

metrics.maturity: Explained in a private CEO map

spires.abstract: A project status canvas: epics, waiting items, a risk cascade and milestones. A different kind of document — a plan, not a text — explained with the same kit.

spires.title: Discovery agent

metrics.acceleration: Reads the source, proposes the metaphor

spires.abstract: Reads the source document and proposes the city: the axis, the districts, the landmarks, the bottlenecks, the flows. Output is a short domain profile a human can review in minutes.

spires.title: Domain profile
spires.abstract: The first gate: one page that states how the document will be mapped and why. Cheap to argue about before anything is built.

spires.title: Architect agent
spires.abstract: Turns the approved profile into a city spec: stations, flows, constraints, priorities, tour — with no coordinates. Rules in the prompt: numbers only from the source, constraints placed where they act.

spires.title: City spec

metrics.acceleration: Districts · spires · roads · constraints · tour · metro

spires.abstract: The contract between understanding and building. Pure semantics — what exists, what flows where, what blocks what, what the tour says — and every view and every voice is generated from it.

spires.title: Human review & provenance

metrics.acceleration: Paper vs derived vs map choice

spires.abstract: A person approves the profile and the spec, and a provenance file separates what the source says, what was recounted, and what is a choice of the map. It caught a claim in the paper that its own data do not support.

spires.title: Spatial compiler
spires.abstract: Deterministic: validates references, places buildings, routes roads, derives traffic, queues, weather, the metro layout and the tour cameras. No coordinates are ever written by hand unless asked.

spires.title: City view
spires.abstract: Districts, buildings whose shape says what a thing is, roads with traffic and barriers, data tables painted on the ground.

spires.title: Metro view

metrics.scale: SVG schematic from the same spec

spires.abstract: For readers who find the city too busy: the same spec as a metro map — lines per district, compact interchanges with an explanation card, labels that never overlap.

spires.title: Guided tour

metrics.maturity: Nine stops in the paper map

spires.abstract: A story told with the map: each stop flies the camera, dims everything else and says one thing. The stops are what the voices will read.

spires.title: Validator & render checks
spires.abstract: Refuses a spec with broken references or impossible combinations, and every change is checked by rendering it headless before it ships.

spires.title: deckcast
spires.abstract: Compiles a narration script into voiced clips with a cache, measures them and builds a timeline — a video, or per-page audio with line-level cues for a web player.

spires.title: Narration script
spires.abstract: The handover between the map and the voices: one page per tour stop, one line per spoken sentence, two speakers.

spires.title: Audio & cues

metrics.scale: One mp3 per stop + line timings

spires.abstract: Lets the player show subtitles and fire map actions exactly when a line is spoken.

spires.title: Level 1 — narrated dialogue tour
spires.abstract: The tour read as a conversation: the sceptic asks what a reviewer would ask, the guide answers and points at the map.

spires.title: Level 2 — questions to choose
spires.abstract: Click a question, the tour pauses, a recorded answer plays and the map shows the evidence, then the tour continues.

spires.title: Level 3 — talk to the city

metrics.acceleration: Knowledge = the spec; tools = map actions

spires.abstract: Ask anything by voice; the agent answers from the map's own knowledge and flies the camera to the evidence.

spires.title: SCIANCE materials map
spires.abstract: The materials-science chapter as a city with constraints drawn where they act.

spires.title: Autoresearch in the Wild
spires.abstract: The paper as five story districts with lineages, failure modes, six rules on trial, data plazas and a provenance file.

spires.title: Knowledge Discovery CEO view
spires.abstract: A project as a time corridor with a 'you are here' line; kept private because it names people and risks.

spires.title: deckcast narrated decks
spires.abstract: Two decks already narrated end to end, one with a talk-to-the-agent link.

bottlenecks.title: A person must check the spec
bottlenecks.impact: Agents draft the profile and the spec, but numbers and claims need a human read before publishing; the paper map's provenance file exists for that reason.
bottlenecks.remedy: Keep the two gates and the provenance file; make the review a checklist.

bottlenecks.title: Dense maps need manual placement
bottlenecks.impact: Automatic placement handles small districts; districts with many buildings or plazas still need explicit positions in the spec.
bottlenecks.remedy: Smarter packing in the compiler; label placement already avoids overlaps.

bottlenecks.title: Narration scripts are written by hand
bottlenecks.impact: deckcast compiles a script but does not write it; the tour-to-dialogue export is the missing step.
bottlenecks.remedy: Export the tour as a two-voice script, then review it like the spec.

bottlenecks.title: The live agent needs the network
bottlenecks.impact: A live voice agent adds latency and can be unreachable during a demo.
bottlenecks.remedy: Levels 1 and 2 work offline from files; the mic button hides itself when the agent is unreachable.

challenges.title: Minutes, not pages
challenges.target: Understand a 50-page document's argument in a five-minute guided tour — and still be able to open every number.

challenges.title: Every number traceable
challenges.target: Each station says where its numbers come from: the source, a recount, or a choice of the map.

challenges.title: One spec, every view
challenges.target: City, metro, tour and voices are all generated from the same spec, so they never disagree.

challenges.title: Ask the city
challenges.target: Anyone can ask a question by voice and be shown the answer on the map.
